items.followUp: Define Dobereiner’s Triads and give a suitable example with the atomic masses.

rubric.why: A triad is a group of three elements with similar chemical properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a triad as three elements with similar chemical properties.

rubric.why: In the Li, Na and K triad, the middle element’s atomic mass is approximately the average of the other two.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid triad example and its approximate average-mass relationship.

modelAnswer: Dobereiner’s Triads are groups of three elements with similar chemical properties, in which the atomic mass of the middle element is approximately the average of the other two.
For example, in Li, Na and K, the atomic mass of Na (23) is approximately the average of Li (7) and K (39): (7 + 39) / 2 = 23.

items.followUp: State the trend in electron affinity across a period and give a reason.

rubric.why: Electron affinity generally decreases in magnitude down a group and becomes less negative.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electron affinity generally decreases or becomes less negative down a group.

rubric.why: Increasing atomic size or shielding reduces the nucleus’s attraction for an added electron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking increased atomic size or shielding with weaker attraction for an added electron.

modelAnswer: Electron affinity generally decreases down a group (becomes less negative).
Down a group, atomic size and shielding increase, so the nucleus attracts an added electron less strongly.
